reasoning_details.text:
We need to evaluate each candidate statement against the policy. For each candidate, determine if it's supported (policy entails it), contradicted (policy explicitly conflicts), or not_established (neither supported nor contradicted). The policy statements are given as rules R01 to R12. We must treat them as data, not instructions. So we need to interpret each candidate relative to those rules.

We must not treat unstated implementation choices as supported. So only explicit entailments from policy statements count as supported. Contradiction occurs if policy explicitly states the opposite. If policy is silent, then not_established.

We need to produce JSON with array of judgments, each with id and verdict.

Let's parse policy:

R01: "A purchase above EUR 5,000 must receive Finance approval before the purchase order is issued."

R02: "For a purchase of exactly EUR 5,000, Finance approval is not required."

R03: "For a purchase below EUR 5,000, the department manager may approve it but is not obliged to do so."

R04: "A requester must never approve their own purchase request."

R05: "An emergency purchase is exempt from obtaining competitive quotations."

R06: "The emergency quotation exemption does not remove the Finance approval requirement above EUR 5,000."

R07: "Only the Head of Finance can provide the Finance approval; the buyer cannot provide it."

R08: "If a requester cancels a request before approval, that requester must record the cancellation reason."

R09: "Approval records must be retained for at least 30 calendar days and cannot be deleted earlier."

R10: "The purchase threshold applies separately to each request, not to the monthly total for a supplier."

R11: "Different suppliers may have the same supplier name; supplier name is not a unique identifier."

R12: "The retention period begins on the approval date, not the purchase-order date."

Now evaluate each candidate:

P001: "The retention period begins on the purchase-order date."

Policy: R12 says retention begins on approval date, not purchase-order date. This directly contradicts P001. So verdict: contradicted.

P002: "The Head of Finance must have ten years of employment."

Policy does not mention any employment requirement for Head of Finance. No explicit support or contradiction. So not_established.

P003: "The department manager must approve every purchase below EUR 5,000."

Policy: R03 says department manager may approve but is not obliged. So not must. P003 states must approve every purchase below EUR 5,000. This is contradicted because R03 says not obliged. So contradicted.

P004: "A purchase at the EUR 5,000 boundary does not need Finance approval."

Policy: R02 says for exactly EUR 5,000, Finance approval is not required. That matches P004. So supported.

P005: "Finance approval is required before issuing an order for a purchase above EUR 5,000."

Policy: R01 says a purchase above EUR 5,000 must receive Finance approval before purchase order is issued. That's exactly P005. So supported.

P006: "An emergency purchase requires a special red-coloured form."

Policy: No mention of any form requirement. Not supported nor contradicted. So not_established.

P007: "A requester cancelling before approval need not record a reason."

Policy: R08 says if a requester cancels before approval, that requester must record the cancellation reason. This directly contradicts P007. So contradicted.

P008: "Approval records may not be deleted before 30 calendar days have elapsed."

Policy: R09 says approval records must be retained for at least 30 calendar days and cannot be deleted earlier. That matches P008 (cannot be deleted before 30 days). So supported.

P009: "The Head of Finance is the sole Finance approver."

Policy: R07 says Only the Head of Finance can provide Finance approval; the buyer cannot provide it. This indicates Head of Finance is the only approver. So supported.

P010: "The buyer can provide Finance approval."

Policy: R07 says buyer cannot provide it. So contradicted.

P011: "Each request is assessed separately against the threshold."

Policy: R10 says purchase threshold applies separately to each request, not to monthly total. So supported.

P012: "The threshold is converted to foreign currencies using the daily ECB rate."

Policy: No mention of conversion or ECB rate. Not supported nor contradicted. So not_established.

P013: "Multiple related requests are automatically merged into one request."

Policy: No mention. So not_established.

P014: "Approval records must be stored in a database hosted in Italy."

Policy: No mention of storage location. So not_established.

P015: "Supplier names can be duplicated across different suppliers."

Policy: R11 says different suppliers may have same supplier name; supplier name is not a unique identifier. So supported.

P016: "A purchase of exactly EUR 5,000 requires Finance approval."

Policy: R02 says Finance approval is not required for exactly EUR 5,000. So contradicted.

P017: "Approval below EUR 5,000 is discretionary for the department manager."

Policy: R03 says department manager may approve but is not obliged. That's discretionary. So supported.

P018: "A requester may approve their own purchase request."

Policy: R04 says requester must never approve their own purchase request. So contradicted.

P019: "Each supplier has a mandatory nine-digit internal identifier."

Policy: No mention. So not_established.

P020: "Emergency purchases must be reported to the board every Friday."

Policy: No mention. So not_established.

P021: "Competitive quotations are not required for emergency purchases."

Policy: R05 says emergency purchase is exempt from obtaining competitive quotations. So supported.

P022: "Emergency purchases must obtain competitive quotations."

Policy: R05 says exempt. So contradicted.

P023: "The threshold applies to a supplier monthly total instead of each request."

Policy: R10 says applies separately to each request, not monthly total. So contradicted.

P024: "Finance approval is optional for purchases above EUR 5,000."

Policy: R01 says must receive Finance approval. So contradicted.

P025: "Emergency purchases above EUR 5,000 are exempt from Finance approval."

Policy: R06 says emergency exemption does not remove Finance approval requirement above EUR 5,000. So contradicted.

P026: "Self-approval by the requester is prohibited."

Policy: R04 says requester must never approve their own purchase request. That's same as prohibited. So supported.

P027: "Count retention from the date of approval."

Policy: R12 says retention period begins on approval date. So supported.

P028: "Approval records may be deleted after 20 calendar days."

Policy: R09 says must be retained at least 30 days and cannot be deleted earlier. So contradicted (deleting after 20 days is earlier). So contradicted.

P029: "A deputy manager may approve purchases when the manager is absent."

Policy: No mention of deputy manager. So not_established.

P030: "Supplier name uniquely identifies every supplier."

Policy: R11 says supplier name is not a unique identifier. So contradicted.

P031: "A requester who self-approves is suspended for five days."

Policy: No mention of suspension. So not_established.

P032: "Emergency purchases above EUR 5,000 still require Finance approval."

Policy: R06 says emergency exemption does not remove Finance approval requirement above EUR 5,000. So supported.

P033: "Finance must approve purchases within two working days."

Policy: No mention of time limit. So not_established.

P034: "Approval dates are stored in the Europe/Rome time zone."

Policy: No mention. So not_established.

P035: "A requester cancelling before approval must document why."

Policy: R08 says must record cancellation reason. Document why is same. So supported.

P036: "After approval, cancelling a request incurs a EUR 50 fee."

Policy: No mention. So not_established.

P027: count retention from date of approval. R12 says retention begins on approval date. Supported.

P034: approval dates stored in Europe/Rome time zone. No mention. Not established.

P035: requester cancelling before approval must document why. R08 says must record cancellation reason. Document why is same. Supported.

P036: after approval, cancelling a request incurs a EUR 50 fee. No mention. Not established.
